defs.def: A paragraph or section of text or music with particular meaning.
defs.example: She struggled to play the difficult passages.

defs.def: Part of a path or journey.
defs.example: He made his passage through the trees carefully, mindful of the stickers.

defs.def: An incident or episode.
The official approval of a bill or act by a parliament.
defs.example: The company was one of the prime movers in lobbying for the passage of the act.

defs.def: The advance of time.
The use of tight brushwork to link objects in separate spatial plains. Commonly seen in Cubist works.
A passageway or corridor.
An underground cavity, formed by water or falling rocks, which is much longer than it is wide.
The vagina.
The act of passing; movement across or through.
The right to pass from one place to another.
A fee paid for passing or for being conveyed between places.
Serial passage, a technique used in bacteriology and virology
A gambling game for two players using three dice, in which the object is to throw a double over ten.
A sentence, phrase or word which asks for information, reply or response; an interrogative.
defs.example: What is your question?

defs.def: A subject or topic for consideration or investigation.
defs.example: The question of seniority will be discussed at the meeting.

defs.def: A doubt or challenge about the truth or accuracy of a matter.
defs.example: He obeyed without question.

defs.def: A proposal to a meeting as a topic for deliberation.
defs.example: I move that the question be put to a vote.

defs.def: (chiefly with definite article) Interrogation by torture.
Talk; conversation; speech.
Used as plural of person; a body of human beings considered generally or collectively; a group of two or more persons.
defs.example: There were so many people at the restaurant last night.

defs.def: Persons forming or belonging to a particular group, such as a nation, class, ethnic group, country, family, etc.
A group of persons regarded as being employees, followers, companions or subjects of a ruler.
One's colleagues or employees.
A person's ancestors, relatives or family.
defs.example: My people lived through the Black Plague and the Thirty Years War.

defs.def: The mass of a community as distinguished from a special class (elite); the commonalty; the populace; the vulgar; the common crowd; the citizens.
In good health.
defs.example: I had been sick, but now I'm well.

defs.def: Good, content.
defs.example: “How are you?” — “I'm well, thank you!”

defs.def: Prudent; good; well-advised.
Moving around; astir.
defs.example: After my bout with Guillan-Barre Syndrome, it took me 6 months to be up and about again.

defs.def: In existence; being in evidence; apparent.
defs.example: This idea has been about for a while but has only recently become fashionable.

defs.def: Near; in the vicinity or neighbourhood.
defs.example: I had my keys just a minute ago, so they must be about somewhere.

defs.def: A response or reply; something said or done in reaction to a statement or question.
defs.example: Her answer to his proposal was a slap in the face.

defs.def: A solution to a problem.
defs.example: There is no simple answer to corruption.

defs.def: A document filed in response to a complaint, responding to each point raised in the complaint and raising counterpoints.
Brand or kind; model.
defs.example: What make of car do you drive?

defs.def: Manner or style of construction (style of how a thing is made); form.
Origin (of a manufactured article); manufacture; production.
defs.example: The camera was of German make.

defs.def: A person's character or disposition.
The act or process of making something, especially in industrial manufacturing.
Quantity produced, especially of materials.
A software utility for automatically building large applications, or an implementation of this utility.
Identification or recognition (of identity), especially from police records or evidence.
(usually in phrase "easy make") Past, present or future target of seduction (usually female).
A promotion.
A home-made project
Turn to declare the trump for a hand (in bridge), or to shuffle the cards.
A made basket.
The closing of an electrical circuit.
The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events.
defs.example: Time stops for nobody.   the ebb and flow of time

defs.def: A duration of time.
An instant of time.
The measurement under some system of region of day or moment.
defs.example: Let's synchronize our watches so we're not on different time.

defs.def: Ratio of comparison.
defs.example: your car runs three times faster than mine;  that is four times as heavy as this

defs.def: (grammar) Tense.
defs.example: the time of a verb

defs.def: The measured duration of sounds; measure; tempo; rate of movement; rhythmical division.
defs.example: common or triple time;   the musician keeps good time.

defs.def: A chance to speak; the right or power to influence or make a decision.
To pronounce.
defs.example: Please say your name slowly and clearly.

defs.def: To recite.
defs.example: Martha, will you say the Pledge of Allegiance?

defs.def: To tell, either verbally or in writing.
defs.example: He said he would be here tomorrow.

defs.def: To indicate in a written form.
defs.example: The sign says it’s 50 kilometres to Paris.

defs.def: To have a common expression; used in singular passive voice or plural active voice to indicate a rumor or well-known fact.
defs.example: They say "when in Rome, do as the Romans do", which means "behave as those around you do."

defs.def: Suppose, assume; used to mark an example, supposition or hypothesis.
defs.example: A holiday somewhere warm – Florida, say – would be nice.

defs.def: To speak; to express an opinion; to make answer; to reply.
(of a possession, especially money) To bet as a wager on an outcome; by extension, used to express belief in an outcome by the speaker.
(heading) Employment.
(heading) Effort.
Sustained effort to achieve a goal or result, especially overcoming obstacles.
defs.example: We don't have much time. Let's get to work piling up those sandbags.

defs.def: (heading) Product; the result of effort.
The staging of events to appear as real.
Ore before it is dressed.
The equipment needed to inject a drug (syringes, needles, swabs etc.)
defs.example: Tell me you're using clean works at least.

defs.def: (modal, auxiliary verb, defective) Used before a verb to indicate the simple future tense in the first person singular or plural.
defs.example: I hope that we shall win the game.

defs.def: Used similarly to indicate determination or obligation in the second and third persons singular or plural.
defs.example: (determination): You shall go to the ball!

defs.def: Used in questions with the first person singular or plural to suggest a possible future action.
defs.example: Let us examine that, shall we?

defs.def: To owe.
A portion; a component.
Duty; responsibility.
defs.example: to do one’s part

defs.def: The dividing line formed by combing the hair in different directions.
defs.example: The part of his hair was slightly to the left.

defs.def: In the Hebrew lunisolar calendar, a unit of time equivalent to 3⅓ seconds.
A constituent of character or capacity; quality; faculty; talent; usually in the plural with a collective sense.
The act of using.
defs.example: The use of torture has been condemned by the United Nations.

defs.def: The act of consuming alcohol or narcotics.
(followed by "of") Usefulness, benefit.
defs.example: What's the use of a law that nobody follows?

defs.def: A function; a purpose for which something may be employed.
defs.example: This tool has many uses.

defs.def: Occasion or need to employ; necessity.
defs.example: I have no further use for these textbooks.

defs.def: Interest for lent money; premium paid for the use of something; usury.
Continued or repeated practice; usage; habit.
Common occurrence; ordinary experience.
The special form of ritual adopted for use in any diocese.
defs.example: the Sarum, or Canterbury, use; the Hereford use; the York use; the Roman use; etc.

defs.def: (forging) A slab of iron welded to the side of a forging, such as a shaft, near the end, and afterward drawn down, by hammering, so as to lengthen the forging.
(sometimes attributive) In billiards and similar games, a stroke causing a ball to follow another ball after hitting it.
defs.example: a follow shot

defs.def: The act of following another user's online activity.
To go after; to pursue; to move behind in the same path or direction.
defs.example: Follow that car!

defs.def: To go or come after in a sequence.
defs.example: B follows A in the alphabet.

defs.def: To carry out (orders, instructions, etc.).
defs.example: Follow these instructions to the letter.

defs.def: To live one's life according to (religion, teachings, etc).
To understand, to pay attention to.
defs.example: Do you follow me?

defs.def: To watch, to keep track of (reports of) some event or person.
defs.example: I followed the incumbent throughout the election.

defs.def: To subscribe to see content from an account on a social media platform.
defs.example: If you want to see more of our articles, follow us on Twitter.

defs.def: To be a logical consequence of something.
defs.example: If you don't practise proper hygiene, illness is sure to follow.

defs.def: To walk in, as a road or course; to attend upon closely, as a profession or calling.
A solar year, the time it takes the Earth to complete one revolution of the Sun (between 365.24 and 365.26 days depending on the point of reference).
defs.example: we moved to this town a year ago;  I quit smoking exactly one year ago

defs.def: (by extension) The time it takes for any astronomical object (such as a planet, dwarf planet, small Solar System body, or comet) in direct orbit around a star (such as the Sun) to make one revolution around the star.
defs.example: Mars goes around the sun once in a Martian year, or 1.88 Earth years.

defs.def: A period between set dates that mark a year, from January 1 to December 31 by the Gregorian calendar, from Tishiri 1 to Elul 29 by the Jewish calendar, and from Muharram 1 to Dhu al-Hijjah 29 or 30 by the Islamic calendar.
defs.example: A normal year has 365 full days, but there are 366 days in a leap year.

defs.def: A scheduled part of a calendar year spent in a specific activity.
defs.example: During this school year I have to get up at 6:30 to catch the bus.

defs.def: A Julian year, exactly 365.25 days, represented by "a".
A level or grade in school or college.
defs.example: Every second-year student must select an area of specialization.

defs.def: The proportion of a creature's lifespan equivalent to one year of an average human lifespan (see also dog year).
defs.example: Geneticists have created baker's yeast that can live to 800 in yeast years.
